claim_text: Hugendubel says it was hit by a hacker attack on its IT systems in the night of Nov 18 to 19, 2026
summary: A spokesperson for Hugendubel told the German news agency dpa that there was a hacker attack on the company's IT systems in the night from Wednesday to Thursday (Nov 18 to 19), and that the company switched everything off at once.
detail: The statement is quoted in dpa's own report as carried by Handelsblatt, and repeated by Golem.de, retail-news.de, BR24 and the dpa wire on Süddeutsche Zeitung. Golem adds that, per the company, the outage was deliberately brought about by Hugendubel itself. A spokesperson also told F.A.Z. directly that the attack happened that night. Outlets repeating this one statement count as one source. No independent party has yet confirmed the attack.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own on-record statement, read directly in the dpa report on Handelsblatt, says it was a hacker attack.
notes: Gap: the company's own web notice and help pages say only 'technical disruption' (c002). The attack wording comes from the spokesperson's statements to dpa and F.A.Z. and, per heise, from Hugendubel's own Instagram post, which we have not read directly.

claim_text: Until Nov 23, Hugendubel's own website notice and help pages called the outage a 'technical disruption' and did not mention an attack
summary: Until our Nov 23 read, the notice on hugendubel.de and the tolino cloud help page said the shop, cloud and service center were unreachable because of a 'technische Störung'. By Nov 24 both said 'cyberattack'.
detail: We read both pages ourselves on Nov 22. Neither mentions a cyberattack, hackers or ransomware. Until the pages changed, the answer to the main question rested on the spokesperson's statement to dpa alone.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: Both company pages were read directly on Nov 22 and Nov 23 and used that wording then.

claim_text: Hugendubel took its systems offline itself as a precaution
summary: The spokesperson said 'everything was taken off the network at once'; retail-news.de and Golem.de report the systems were switched off deliberately to prevent further damage.
detail: This is the company's description. Nothing public shows what the attackers did before or after the switch-off.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One company statement relayed by dpa and outlets; not independently checked.

claim_text: The Hugendubel web shop, the tolino cloud and the service center are offline
summary: hugendubel.de returned an error page (HTTP 503) on Nov 22 with the company's notice that the online shop, the tolino cloud and the service center are unreachable. The company says its stores remain open.
detail: DerWesten and dpa report the site has been unreachable since Thursday, Nov 19. The notice does not give a restoration time. F.A.Z. reported on Sunday, Nov 22, that hugendubel.de still showed only the outage notice.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own live notice, read directly on Nov 22, plus the help page and dpa.

claim_text: Tolino cloud: purchased e-books that are not already on a device cannot be downloaded, and sync and Family Sharing are down
summary: Hugendubel's help page says the tolino cloud is unreachable, so downloads not already made, downloads to e-readers, apps and the web reader, and sync of reading position, notes and Family Sharing are all unavailable.
detail: The help page was last changed on Fri, Nov 20. It concerns Hugendubel's own tolino cloud. Whether customers of other tolino bookshops are affected is not stated in anything we read.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own help page, read directly.
notes: heise online (Nov 23) adds that firmware updates are still offered to e-readers, because they come from servers outside the tolino cloud.

claim_text: E-books already downloaded to a device still work
summary: Hugendubel's help center says e-books already saved on a device can still be read, and books already downloaded to a computer can be copied to a tolino by cable.
detail: Netzwelt and retail-news.de reported this first. The company's own help article, changed Nov 25, now says it directly.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's help article says e-books already stored on the device can still be read.

claim_text: Hugendubel's email and customer contact are down too
summary: The spokesperson said no emails could be sent, per dpa and DER SPIEGEL. DerWesten and retail-news.de say email traffic and the service center are down. Hugendubel's returns help page confirms free return labels cannot be created online.
detail: The email outage is the company's statement as relayed by dpa. The return-label part is on the company's own help page (see c014). BR24 adds that the company could not use its email accounts. A spokesperson told F.A.Z. that email traffic is affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: Company statement relayed by dpa and outlets.

claim_text: No customer data or other confidential data was stolen, per the company
summary: The spokesperson said 'the good news is that no customer data or other confidential data were stolen', because the company was long prepared with emergency plans and shut everything down at once.
detail: This is the company's claim only. retail-news.de notes there is no independent confirmation and no published technical report. Netzwelt advises customers who reuse a Hugendubel password to change it as a precaution. Caschys Blog reports that Hugendubel is informing affected customers by email, and that the company has given no detail on the kind of attack. A spokesperson told F.A.Z. the same, saying the company's long-standing emergency mechanisms worked. In the company's Instagram post, as quoted by heise, Hugendubel hedges: 'according to current knowledge' no sensitive or personal customer data are affected.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One company statement, relayed by several outlets; not checked by anyone else.
notes: On Nov 24 the company's own website notice said that, as of that day, no sensitive or personal customer data is affected (see the newer claim).

claim_text: Whether it was ransomware
summary: No public source says malware or encryption was used. retail-news.de says calling it ransomware would currently be speculation, and no demand has been reported.
detail: The company has not said how the systems were hit or whether data was encrypted.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No source states the type of attack.

claim_text: Who is behind the attack
summary: No claim of responsibility and no attribution appears in the sources we read. This page does not name or guess at an attacker.
detail: We did not look at any leak or criminal sites. If a group claims it, we will cite it only through reputable press.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: Nothing public names the attacker.

claim_text: How the attackers got in
summary: The company has published no technical detail on the entry point or the method.
detail: retail-news.de says the method, the identity of the attackers and any demands are unknown.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No technical detail has been published.

claim_text: When the shop, service center and tolino cloud will be restored
summary: The company now says it expects to be reachable again shortly, with no date. Earlier it said the outage could last several more days. The shop was still offline on Nov 25.
detail: 'Shortly' (in Kürze) is the company's estimate on its notice and help center, read Nov 25, not a commitment. Golem.de said there was no information on when systems would run again.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: No date has been given.

claim_text: Whether Hugendubel's physical stores and internal systems are affected
summary: The company says its stores remain open, and a spokesperson told F.A.Z. that the stores and their tills are not affected. retail-news.de says the published information does not show whether the stores' own systems are affected.
detail: The stores-and-tills part is the company's claim only, given to F.A.Z. on Nov 20; no independent source has checked it. No source reports store disruption. Whether internal systems beyond the shop, cloud, service center and email were hit is not published.
label: Not established
why_it_supports: The company's notice says stores are open and its spokesperson says stores and tills are unaffected; nobody else has checked, and nothing is published about internal systems.

claim_text: Hugendubel now offers free return labels through a link on its help page, and has extended the return deadline
summary: Hugendubel's returns help page, changed Nov 23, links to a free return label (customer or order number as reference). It says returns may be processed late because of the disruption and withdrawal deadlines are extended.
detail: The earlier version of the page (changed Nov 20) said free return labels could not be created. The Nov 23 version says the company is working to offer return labels the usual way again. It gives no new deadline date.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own help page, read directly on Nov 23, states this.

claim_text: LovelyBooks, a Munich book community site, said it was also hit by a cyberattack in the night of Nov 18 to 19
summary: TAG24 reports a LovelyBooks social media post, almost word for word like Hugendubel's: it was hit by a cyberattack in the night of Nov 18 to 19, no personal data are affected so far, and the site may be down for days.
detail: Only one outlet reports this, quoting the LovelyBooks post. Whether the two attacks are linked, share a cause or an attacker, or whether the companies are related is not stated in anything we read. lovelybooks.de could not be reached from our server on Nov 22.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: TAG24 quotes both companies' social media statements side by side.
notes: Same night and near-identical wording; a link between the two is not established.

claim_text: ebook.de, a second online bookshop run by the same Hugendubel company, is offline with the same notice
summary: ebook.de returned an error page (HTTP 503) on Nov 22 with the same notice as hugendubel.de: its online shop, the tolino cloud and its service center are unreachable because of a 'technical disruption'.
detail: The imprint on both notices names the same operator, Hugendubel Digital GmbH & Co. KG in Hamburg. Blogspan first pointed this out; we read the ebook.de notice ourselves. Like the Hugendubel notice, it does not mention an attack. Customers who buy tolino e-books through ebook.de are likely in the same position, but the notice does not say so in those words.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The company's own live notice on ebook.de, read directly on Nov 22.
notes: heise online (Nov 23) also reports ebook.de as down alongside Hugendubel.

claim_text: Other tolino shops such as Thalia are not affected, per heise online
summary: heise online reports that only customers of Hugendubel and its ebook.de brand are affected, because other tolino sellers such as Thalia run their business separately through their own sign-in servers on the platform.
detail: heise states this in its own words without naming a source; neither Hugendubel, Thalia nor the tolino alliance has said it publicly in a source we could read. No other outlet reports Thalia customers having problems.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: One Tier 2 outlet reports it. heise's report is grouped with the outlets relaying the company's statement (group hugendubel-statement), so it counts once, and there is no official statement, so it stays Reported.

claim_text: Hugendubel's own website notice now says it was the target of a cyberattack in the night of Nov 18 to 19
summary: Read on Nov 24: the notice on hugendubel.de says Hugendubel was the target of a cyberattack in the night leading into Nov 19. ebook.de shows the same notice, and the tolino cloud help page blames the cyberattack too.
detail: The notice adds that it may take a few more days before the online shop, the tolino cloud and the service center are reachable again. The notice had said only 'technical disruption' at our Nov 23 read. The help page shows it was changed on Nov 24. This is the company's own account, not an independent finding; it names no attacker or method.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: We read the company's own homepage notice, its second shop's notice and its help page directly; all three use the word cyberattack.

claim_text: Hugendubel's website notice says that, as of Nov 24, no sensitive or personal customer data is affected
summary: The notice on hugendubel.de, read on Nov 24, says that as things stand that day no sensitive or personal data of its customers is affected. ebook.de's notice says the same.
detail: This is the company's own statement about its own investigation so far, and it is worded as of that day. Nothing independent backs it yet.
label: Confirmed
why_it_supports: The sentence is on the company's own notice, read directly. It confirms what the company says, not that no data was taken.

claim_text: Hugendubel says the attackers could not copy or encrypt any data
summary: The company's help center, changed Nov 25, answers 'Are my data affected?' with: no, the attackers could not copy or encrypt any data, and customers need do nothing.
detail: This is the company's own statement; no outside party has confirmed it. It goes further than the Nov 24 notice (c019), which said no sensitive or personal data was affected as things stood.
label: Reported
why_it_supports: The help article states that the attackers could not copy or encrypt data.
